description: ALUES is an R model for scoring land suitability for different crops. The developers implement a fuzzy-logic evaluation of land units against crop requirements using rainfall, temperature, topography and soil properties. The JOSS article reports example input land units for Marinduque in the Philippines and Lao Cai in Vietnam; those examples do not establish global validation. Spatial resolution is the supplied land unit, and the temporal period follows the climate and soil inputs. The package is public on GitHub, and its DESCRIPTION states MIT, so the software is free. Food-supply modellers could use suitability scores when testing possible crop-area shifts or agricultural production constraints. A suitability score is not a harvested-yield forecast, and it omits farm management, irrigation rights, markets and land-use policy unless those are supplied separately. Input quality and crop requirement thresholds govern the ranking. No matching catalogue or first-review record was found. The JOSS paper and own package metadata were read without running the examples. No directly related catalogue record was established.
